us_person.explanation: UK general investment account is transparent for US tax, but non-US pooled holdings inside it are PFIC candidates and UK/US basis, timing and FX differences create double-reporting friction.
sources: UK/US DTA 2001 Art. 24 (relief from double taxation)

uk_resident.explanation: Standard UK taxable account: dividends, interest and gains taxed per UK rules.

us_person.explanation: ISA is UK tax-free but has no US treaty recognition: income and gains are US-taxable annually, and fund holdings inside are PFIC candidates. Annual US drag estimated where holdings data allows.

uk_resident.explanation: Income and gains free of UK tax.

us_person.explanation: Treated as a treaty-recognised pension: growth deferral generally available under Art. 17/18 positions. Badge carries stated assumptions; PFIC exposure inside the wrapper flagged WARN with wrapper context, not CRITICAL.
sources: IRS Rev. Proc. 2014-55 analogy (position, not authority)

uk_resident.explanation: Registered pension scheme: relief on contributions within allowances, tax-free growth, PCLS within Lump Sum Allowance.

us_person.explanation: UK insurance bond held by a US person: underlying funds are PFIC-in-a-wrapper, the policy may fail IRC s7702 life-insurance definition (taxed as investment), and insurer-level 953(d) issues can apply. Flag only — no advice text.

uk_resident.explanation: Chargeable event regime: 5% cumulative withdrawal allowance, top-slicing relief; gains taxed as income with basic-rate credit.

us_person.explanation: Offshore bond held by a US person: PFIC-in-a-wrapper plus potential s7702 failure; no US recognition of the UK chargeable-event regime. Flag only — no advice text.

uk_resident.explanation: Chargeable event regime without basic-rate credit; gross roll-up inside the bond.

us_person.explanation: Standard US taxable brokerage; US-registered funds are not PFICs.
sources: IRC s1297 (US-registered funds out of scope)

uk_resident.explanation: US-domiciled funds/ETFs held by a UK resident are usually non-reporting funds: gains taxed as offshore income gains at income rates unless the share class has UK reporting-fund status. Check the bundled HMRC list.

us_person.explanation: US tax-deferred retirement account; distributions taxed as income.

uk_resident.explanation: Treaty pension: UK generally recognises deferral under Art. 17/18; lump-sum vs periodic distribution treatment differs — noted per treaty position.
Treaty position generally preserves US tax-free character for UK residents under Art. 17(1)(b); stated as a modelling assumption.
Treaty-recognised pension for UK residents (Art. 17/18); US-situs for estate purposes — split out in the situs table.

us_person.explanation: US education savings plan; tax-free for qualified education expenses.

uk_resident.explanation: No UK recognition: growth potentially taxable to a UK-resident owner; underlying funds may be offshore funds for UK purposes.
sources: No UK/US DTA provision for s529 plans

us_person.explanation: Non-US accounts count toward FBAR/Form 8938 thresholds; interest US-taxable.

uk_resident.explanation: Interest taxable within personal savings allowance rules.

us_person.explanation: Non-US accounts count toward FBAR/Form 8938 thresholds; interest US-taxable. Cash ISAs additionally carry the ISA WARN.

uk_resident.explanation: Interest taxable within personal savings allowance rules.

us_person.explanation: US persons are taxable on worldwide property income/gains; s121 exclusion and UK PPR relief interact imperfectly; FX gain on repaying a foreign mortgage can be US-taxable.

uk_resident.explanation: UK property taxed per UK rules; main residence relief may apply.

us_person.explanation: Non-US private companies can trigger CFC or PFIC status and Form 5471/8621 filings depending on ownership and asset/income mix — flagged needs_classification for operator review.

uk_resident.explanation: Unlisted holdings: valuation is operator-supplied; BADR/IHT business relief positions out of scope in v0.
